_README: Judgment inputs for the Risk tab. scripts/gen_risk_json.py reads this, joins it to
the live IBKR book (data/ibkr_flex.json) and live prices, and writes prototypes/risk.json.
EVERYTHING IN THIS FILE IS A HUMAN DECISION. Nothing here is refreshed by the pipeline.
The generator recomputes only what is unambiguously price-driven: marks, stop distances,
vol, ATR, touch probabilities, VaR, correlation, gross, stop_total and the budget meters.
Stops: an Activity Flex Query has 47 sections and none report working orders, so the
unattended pipeline cannot read a GTC stop. The IBKR MCP connector can, but only inside
a Claude session: scripts/ibkr_mcp_import.py turns that read into data/ibkr_live.json,
and while it is the fresher book gen_risk_json.py takes positions AND stops from it.
The stops below are the FALLBACK for runs that only have Flex - copy them from the
latest MCP read. A holding takes one `stop` plus the `qty` it was set against, or
`stops` as [{qty, stop}] tranches that must cover the whole position. Either way a
resized position is refused until its stops are re-read.
scenarios / slippage / gap are authored at the prices in price_basis against the
positions in basis_book. They do NOT auto-update - the betas behind each row are
documented below, and the generator will not recompute or invent them. When live
prices drift past drift_tolerance, or the live book differs from basis_book, the
output carries judgment_stale=true and the tab says so. Re-derive them, update
basis_book and price_basis, and bump reviewed_on.
Derivations for the 7 Oct 2026 book (FPS 1,000, GOOGL 200, META 100, MSFT 137, SOXL 120,
UNG 3,000), at the 6 Oct regular-session closes in price_basis:
Natural gas -20%: UNG at beta 1.0 to front-month gas. -20% takes UNG to 8.59, through
both 9.35 tranches, so clean fill = the stop distance; gap = UNG market value x 0.20.
Mega-cap tech -10%: MSFT, META and GOOGL at beta 1.0. All three stops (7.2%, 3.5%
and 3.6% below the mark) are inside the move, so clean fills = the three stop distances.
Semiconductors -10%: SOXL at its 60-bar beta to ^SOX, 2.9954 (corr 0.996) => -30%,
through the 129 stop.
AI power infrastructure -10%: FPS at beta 1.0; its 38.50 stop is 6.9% below the mark.
Broad market -3%: 60-bar OLS betas to SPX on simple daily returns, 2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06 - FPS 3.6936,
GOOGL 1.4645, META 1.1706, MSFT 1.9715, SOXL 7.3117. FPS, GOOGL, META and SOXL breach their
stops; MSFT (-5.9% vs a stop 7.2% below) does not and takes its full move. UNG's
beta is -0.26: no hedge credit, so UNG contributes nothing to the row.
Rates +50bp: regressions of daily returns on daily ^TNX changes in bp - 3 years (n=756)
for every name except FPS, which has only 167 observations since its Feb 2026 listing.
Negative point slopes are applied, positive ones get no credit: FPS -0.216%/bp (t -2.36)
=> -10.8%, through its stop; GOOGL -0.0052%/bp (t -0.40, not significant) => -0.26%.
theme_loss is the worst single theme's clean-fill loss in the row.
Gap cases: each name's own scenario move with the stop giving nothing. Alternatives,
not additive - except that MSFT, META and GOOGL share an estimated 28 Oct report date,
which is its own case.
Slippage: UNG's two 9.35 tranches fill x below the stop, floored at the -20% gap price
(8.592) - the 10% row hits the floor.

news.title: MSFT, META and GOOGL all estimated to report on 28 Oct - none confirmed
news.body: Earnings calendars estimate Wednesday 28 Oct for Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet, based on past schedules; none has confirmed. All three sit in the MAG7 theme, so a shared report day is one event for the theme: a -10% gap in all three costs $21,594 against a $6,000 theme cap, and stops do not protect through a scheduled report.

news.title: EIA: 64 Bcf injection; surplus to the five-year average narrows
news.body: For the week to 25 Sep the EIA reported a 64 Bcf net injection. Working gas reached 3,415 Bcf: 79 Bcf (2.4%) above the five-year average, down from 95 Bcf a week earlier, and 138 Bcf (3.9%) below a year ago. Next report: Thu 8 Oct.
news.src: EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report, released 1 Oct 2026 (https://ir.eia.gov/ngs/ngs.html)

news.title: SOXL +6.5% on 2 Oct; no single catalyst confirmed
news.body: SOXL closed at 163.71 on 2 Oct, up 6.5% from 153.69, 6.3% above the 154.00 entry. No company or sector announcement explaining the day's move was confirmed in the sources checked. SOXL resets its 3x leverage daily, so over several days its move can differ materially from 3x the index.

notes: NAV is $300,000 throughout - the notional mandate assigned by the firm. Never measured against account equity, by instruction. 1% = $3,000.
Limits are provisional, set 15 Sep 2026: 2% maximum loss per theme, 6% across the portfolio. Not a written company risk policy.
Themes are assigned, not fed. IBKR returns no sector tags; every theme in this file is a stated assumption.

Stop distances are shown as probability of being touched over a holding period, not in daily sigma - these are GTC orders with no expiry. The probability is the reflection-principle first-passage estimate 2*Phi(-ln(S/B)/(sigma*sqrt(T))) on realised daily vol, zero drift.

Stops are the account's GTC working orders, read through the IBKR connector when the board is refreshed in session; the unattended daily run carries the last read forward, because an IBKR Activity Flex Query cannot report working orders. Where a position has more than one stop, the nearest one drives the touch probabilities and the dollar risk sums every tranche. Still unconfirmed: whether they are enabled outside regular trading hours - most gaps occur overnight, which is exactly when a stop is least likely to help.

Scenario betas: UNG ~1.0 to front-month gas; MSFT, META and GOOGL 1.0 to mega-cap tech; FPS 1.0 to AI power infrastructure; SOXL 3.00 to the SOX (60-bar, corr 0.996 - its daily-reset leverage). Broad-market betas are 60-bar OLS on SPX: FPS 3.69, GOOGL 1.46, META 1.17, MSFT 1.97, SOXL 7.31. MSFT's is inflated by its 30 Jul earnings day (+15.5%; 252-bar beta 0.99). META's 60-bar beta is below its 252-bar 1.45, so if anything its row understates. FPS's and SOXL's 60-bar windows include +13.8% and +24.7% days on 30 Jul. SOXL's breach is also marginal (-21.9% takes it to 128.23 against the 129 stop). META only just breaches its stop in the broad-market row (-3.51% takes it to 712.93 against the 713 stop); MSFT does not breach at all. UNG's market beta is negative (-0.26) and no hedge credit is taken for it.

Scenario, slippage and gap figures are authored at the prices in price_basis (6 Oct regular-session closes) against the positions in basis_book and do not move with the market. The tab flags them when prices drift past tolerance or the book changes.

The MAG7 theme is over its cap on stops alone: MSFT $5,247 + META $2,588 + GOOGL $2,536 = $10,371 of stop risk against the $6,000 theme limit (173%). Adding GOOGL on 6 Oct raised it from 114% on 3 Oct, even after trimming MSFT. That is the limit set on 15 Sep, measured as written; resolving it is the account owner's call, not the board's.

Stops do not protect through a scheduled report. MSFT, META and GOOGL are all estimated to report on 28 Oct (unconfirmed). MSFT's 30 Jul report moved it 15.5% in a day; a -10% gap in all three would cost $21,594, 360% of the theme cap. The gap rows use the -10% scenario, so they are not the worst case.

SOXL is a 3x daily-leveraged fund. The -30% semiconductor row is a one-day shock; over several sessions daily rebalancing makes its path diverge from 3x the index, usually against the holder in a choppy market. Its 129 stop is 21.5% below the mark - about a 7% fall in the SOX.

Rates +50bp is modelled for the first time. FPS has a significant negative slope to yields (-0.216%/bp, t -2.36) - but on only 167 daily observations since its Feb 2026 listing, a period in which AI-infrastructure names and yields may share a common driver, and which includes its +13.8% day on 30 Jul - treat it as indicative. The row also extrapolates a daily slope linearly to a cumulative 50bp move. GOOGL's slope is negative but not significant (-0.0052%/bp, t -0.40). MSFT (+0.020, t 1.82), META (+0.010, t 0.62), SOXL (+0.021, t 0.42) and UNG (+0.019, t 0.78) get no credit. The row excludes TLT (900 shares), which remains the main rate exposure in this account - it falls when yields rise.
Independently reviewed. The first issue (15 Sep 2026) was blocked and reissued; the 27 Sep, 3 Oct and 7 Oct re-derivations were each reviewed the same way before publishing.

Book changes since 3 Oct, from the IBKR trade blotter (get_account_trades, 7 days) read 7 Oct: on 6 Oct MSFT was trimmed 200 -> 137 (33 @ 532.40 and 30 @ 532.305, limit orders, +$2,106.14 realised); UNG added 1,000 @ 10.70 (now 3,000 with two 9.35 stop tranches); FPS opened 1,000 @ about 40.82; GOOGL opened 200 @ 349.05 - all via buy stop-limit entries with the protective stops staged in advance. A pending entry order that has not filled is not on the board. Themes for FPS (AI power infrastructure, set by the account owner 7 Oct) and GOOGL (MAG7) are assigned, not fed. Earlier: GOOGL and GNRC stopped out 23 Sep, SMCI 24 Sep, CRM 25 Sep, SNOW 28 Sep.
